## 固定收益市場主線

科技股再度重挫、油價下跌，但聯準會仍準備收緊政策，美國公債僅小幅回升。10年期殖利率下降0.41個基點至5.1311%，2年期下降1.25個基點至4.8294%。投資人面對更迫切的再融資問題，也開始檢視支撐AI建設熱潮的財務支持，美國高收益債利差明顯擴大。

名目殖利率小幅下滑之際，實質借款成本仍在上升。原油跌約4%，帶動通膨補償下降，10年期實質殖利率卻走高。克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack提出新的警訊：她仍傾向在接連幾次會議小幅升息，但勞動市場已出現轉緊跡象，計畫轉嫁成本的企業也增加。她認為長期通膨預期仍穩固受控，因此政策尚可採取漸進步調。

融資市場則呈現分化。UST Global因投資人需求不足，遭銀行撤回再融資案；Proofpoint開始推介用於收購及延長到期日的債務，Pizza Hut則完成加盟業務支持融資的定價。亞洲方面，新世界發展提出的資本重整方案獲鄭氏家族承諾大額投入，但少數股東將承受嚴重稀釋。中國10月經濟活動數據疲弱，同時出現中期流動性回收與公債下跌，成長不振尚未立即帶來較寬鬆的融資環境。

## 美債稍獲喘息，通膨警訊擴及更多領域

美債漲勢集中在中天期。5年期殖利率下降2.16個基點至4.94%，30年期則上升0.86個基點至5.4741%。2年與10年期利差擴大0.84個基點至30.17個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大2.11個基點至64.47個基點。經過前一週重新定價，較短天期公債稍獲喘息，長債則未跟進回升。

以一週比較，殖利率升幅依然可觀。相較11月9日，2年與5年期分別上升26.79與26.33個基點，10年與30年期分別上升24.91與19.58個基點。近一個月，2年期上升12.11個基點，10年期上升5.83個基點。週一的回落，只抵銷了近期政策敏感借款成本漲幅的一小部分。

實質殖利率與通膨補償走勢分歧。10年期抗通膨公債（TIPS）殖利率上升3.07個基點至2.9154%，損益兩平通膨率則下降3.48個基點至2.2157%。一週以來，實質殖利率上升25.89個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降0.98個基點；近一個月則分別上升19.34與下降13.51個基點。通膨補償回落讓名目公債得以止穩，但長期投資面對的實質折現率仍持續提高。

油價為物價壓力提供明確緩解。WTI期貨下跌3.95%至每桶$85.06，Brent下跌4.17%至$91.84，兩者均較一個月前低約14%。Bloomberg市場報導指出，實體供應充裕與供給過剩擴大的預期，影響超過中東供應中斷疑慮。伊朗再度攻擊巴林，地緣政治風險仍在；不過，外交會談的可能性，加上美國總統川普不願擴大攻擊，減輕了原油的即時上漲壓力。盛寶銀行Ole Sloth Hansen認為，除非緊張情勢造成實際供應損失，否則供給過剩前景的影響更大。

Hammack週一談到可能迫使聯準會偏離漸進緊縮的情況。她在10月會議主張升息而投下反對票，目前仍偏好在接連幾次會議穩定、小幅調升利率。但她指出，若企業與消費者形成通膨心態，可能需要更大的升息幅度，以及更高的最終利率。她評估目前政策利率約在中性水準或略低於中性，仍須進一步收緊，才能抑制邊際投資。

她的疑慮不限於能源與關稅，也包括AI基礎建設及其他成長帶來的需求。更多企業主管討論進一步漲價，部分企業提高較低所得員工的薪資，轄區受訪業者也反映難以找到技術及非技術勞工。對不含住房的核心服務，她特別指出，包含福利與健康保險的完整僱用成本是壓力來源。這些觀察讓通膨擴散的討論，更聚焦於勞動成本。

不過，Hammack認為長期通膨預期仍穩固錨定於聯準會目標附近。市場預期短期升息、長期通膨維持低檔，支持她對政策公信力仍強、官員尚有時間決定步調的判斷。她也不認為恢復物價穩定需要對勞動市場造成重大衝擊：經濟持續強勁成長，企業仍能將成本轉嫁給其他企業，都顯示需求尚未受到約束。

11月紐約州製造業調查同樣呈現活動放緩、資源需求持續的組合。Trading Economics報導，一般商業狀況指數由25.5降至7.8，低於市場預期的18；仍為正值，代表製造業在10月創2021年12月以來最強表現後繼續擴張。新訂單指數由23.2大幅降至3，出貨指數為8.8。

僱用則加速，就業指數由10.3升至18.1，增長速度為四年多來最快，每週工時指數也由9.1升至13.5。支付價格指數由59.5降至45.9，收取價格指數由30.6降至27.2，兩者仍偏高。訂單放緩的同時，勞動需求增強，價格漲勢雖減緩但仍在持續。

供應改善並不一致。交貨時間指數由19.8降至13.8，供應可得性指數由負15.1改善至負9.2；未完成訂單由14降至10.3，庫存由11.6降至9.2。企業對前景更樂觀，未來商業狀況指數由21升至28.9，資本支出計畫由14升至23。整體指數轉弱，為債市提供一項活動降溫訊號，但投資與就業的強度仍呼應Hammack的疑慮。

聯準會主席Kevin Warsh週一另一場談話聚焦AI的不同發展情境。幕僚正在研究三種可能：生產力增益由雇主與勞工共享的擴張；經濟活動增加、卻伴隨大量失業；以及AI發展不如預期，導致股票估值下修、經濟疲弱與失業率上升。他明確將這些界定為情境而非預測，並未直接指引近期利率。聯準會正在評估已可見的AI投資需求，至於效益何時實現、如何分配，仍未定論。

## AI產業的信用支持受到更嚴格檢視

股市跌勢加劇，使AI產業的融資問題更受關注。標普500指數下跌1.92%，Nasdaq 100下跌2.67%，半導體指數下跌5.28%；VIX上升18.70%至22.91。Nvidia股價下跌4.1%，新型雲端業者再度走弱，也使協助它們取得資料中心容量的擔保與租約安排成為焦點。

美國政府對這個產業的國際業務新增具體限制。商務部採取措施，限制中國企業遠端使用先進AI晶片與伺服器。新加坡、馬來西亞、泰國、印尼及巴西的資料中心業者，購買Nvidia及其他美國供應商的半導體將須取得許可。規範不僅涵蓋晶片的實體運送目的地，也觸及運算資源的使用；Nvidia領導層變動後，產業面對的商業問題因而進一步擴大。

川普支持讓黃仁勳復職的呼聲，但CNBC報導，Nvidia董事會並未考慮讓他回任。在這項分歧下，公司策略仍由代理執行長Colette Kress及日後的接任者掌舵。放款機構與出租方關注的核心問題，是新管理團隊將如何支持那些購買Nvidia設備、但自身信用條件較弱的公司。

Bloomberg最新報導指出，早在黃仁勳離職前，Nvidia便已降低承擔完整租約義務的意願，尋求負擔較輕的擔保形式，限制前期資產負債表承諾，以及新型雲端業者無法履約時公司須承擔的義務。Needham分析師John Todaro表示，晶片商的支持已變得更必要，因此這些支持能否延續的不確定性，會影響取得信用融資的能力。

喬治亞州Dalton的洽談顯示了實際限制。據知情人士，今年稍早CoreWeave與Nvidia曾討論由Nvidia承擔租約義務，以協助CoreWeave向Core Scientific取得額外空間，銀行業者也評估圍繞這項安排提供融資，但Nvidia最終未提供支持。AMD隨後依7月與Core Scientific達成的較廣泛協議進駐該空間。

對於這筆未成的交易，CoreWeave表示，是公司自行決定不爭取這些額外容量；它也表示，未曾靠Nvidia或其他夥伴的第三方支持，為資料中心取得投資等級信用增強安排。公司提出的發展路徑，是將目前約1.7吉瓦的已啟用電力容量，增加至2030年超過8吉瓦。Core Scientific則反駁Bloomberg報導，但未進一步說明，並稱客戶多元化一直是業務重點。

出租方的信用條件構成另一道限制。知情人士指出，TeraWulf只接受投資等級租戶，或有藍籌夥伴提供信用支持的租戶；CoreWeave未能滿足條件，因此未獲考慮。Applied Digital去年與CoreWeave簽下大型租約後，正將非投資等級客戶的占比上限設為總容量的30%。租戶信用條件因而直接影響實體容量能否擴張。

CoreWeave週一盤中一度下跌8.6%，Nebius一度下跌9.6%，進一步打擊那些必須先建置容量、再逐步收取客戶收入的公司。Nvidia對不同公司的支持，規模與法律形式差異很大：它承諾投入$20億，協助Nebius採用其基礎設施；也曾討論為Nscale一座預定供Anthropic使用的設施提供信用擔保；對OpenAI向SB Energy承租的俄亥俄州專案，則承諾提供最高$1,050億支持。

新的官方評估將焦點延伸至市場估值以外。聯準會理事Michael Barr在米蘭一場會議的預備講稿中警告，自主AI代理可辨識殖利率差異或金融穩定訊號，並在數分鐘內搬移資金，可能加速存款流失。他表示，大型銀行已偵測到代理試圖在零售帳戶中採取未經授權的行動，建議採用具體的同意驗證程序，並在技術上限制代理能力。Barr也指出，AI基礎建設超過$3兆的表外負債及循環融資安排，都是脆弱環節。

四位聯準會經濟學家的新論文另從總體經濟評估AI。大規模資本支出已影響GDP與物價，對就業的影響則仍小且不一致；近期生產力改善，很大部分早於生成式AI廣泛採用。作者認為，資料中心材料與勞工若長期短缺，可能加重通膨；日後更大的生產力增益，則可能抑制通膨。這也說明，眼前建設需求與未來供給效益，對政策可能有不同意義。

機構配置變化提供了股市下跌之外的另一面。貝萊德將模型投資組合的股票加碼幅度由1%提高至3%，擴大AI曝險、增持較長存續期間的政府債券，並以戰術方式重新增加信用債，尤其是以債券為主的投資組合。主管Target Allocation ETF模型的Michael Gates表示，信用債整體並不便宜，利率也可能持續波動。最近兩個交易日，GOVT流出約$44億、IUSB流出逾$10億，系統化債券基金SYSB則流入約$6億。這些資金重配同時涉及固定收益內部調整及提高股票曝險。

## 亞洲數據疲弱，尚未立即帶來寬鬆

中國10月數據顯示，9月推出支持措施後，經濟動能仍全面減弱。社會消費品零售總額年增僅0.4%，低於市場預期的0.8%；工業生產年增4.8%，增速三個月來首度放緩。1至10月固定資產投資下降8.1%，弱於Bloomberg調查預期的下降7%。Bloomberg Economics估計，單計10月投資年減17%，為疫情之外最深的跌幅。

即使政府已增加舉債額度、推出人民幣8,000億元建設支持計畫，投資仍持續惡化。美銀Helen Qiao認為，刺激政策生效前尚有一段等待期，官員也可能保留部分政策支援，因應2027及2028年更弱的經濟情況。高盛經濟學家指出，10月政府銀行存款異常強勁增長，顯示第4季籌得的部分資金，可能要到2027年初才支出。融資到位與實際支出之間的落差，是財政措施能否扭轉投資下滑的關鍵。

產業結構也顯示，成長仍高度集中於AI相關生產。電子製造業年增近20%，汽車產量卻僅增加0.9%，為疫情結束以來最弱增速。前10個月房地產投資下降21.6%，較前9個月下降20.6%進一步惡化。70城不含保障房的新屋價格月減0.15%，前值為下降0.14%；二手屋價格月減0.24%，前值為下降0.26%。

城鎮調查失業率由5.2%改善至5.1%，但Bloomberg報導引述的經濟學家提醒，這項指標不含失業後返回農村的外來務工者。前三季GDP成長4.6%，第4季只要成長4.3%，即可達到全年4.5%至5%官方目標的下限。這讓官員對活動放緩有一定容忍空間，但成長過度集中的情況，仍使內需受到質疑。

中國人民銀行的流動性操作，對債市傳遞了另一種信號。六個月期買斷式逆回購投放人民幣2,000億元，對應到期量3,000億元；Bloomberg計算，加上先前的三個月期操作，這項工具本月合計淨回收3,000億元，為6月以來首次。銀行隔夜融資利率升至1.30%，高於11月稍早1.25%的六個月低點。10年期公債殖利率上升1個基點至1.62%，30年期公債期貨下跌0.9%，至9月18日以來最低。

東方金誠的王青表示，回收流動性將抑制隔夜利率進一步下滑，避免市場將操作改革解讀為降息。信用事件疑慮也增加壓力：僑銀城市管理曾警告可轉換公司債可能延後償付，其後承諾週二匯出款項。人行週一另透過隔夜逆回購注資；王青認為，年底可能恢復中期資金投放，以配合政府發債與銀行放款。這些操作呈現有選擇的流動性管理，並非單純對疲弱成長數據作出寬鬆反應。

香港則為快速擴張的離岸融資市場增添基礎設施。港交所推出首個債券指數，追蹤在交易所上市、或透過債務工具中央結算系統交收的離岸人民幣債券，由Bloomberg Index Services管理及計算。今年主權與企業點心債發行已達約人民幣1.2兆元，折合$1,750億，超過2025全年。指數推出之際，官方也正推動離岸人民幣殖利率曲線發展，並擴大擔保品用途。

日本GDP呈現消費與投資之間的另一種拉扯。第3季經濟按年率萎縮0.1%，弱於預期的成長0.2%，消費支出下降0.3%，家庭受到惡劣天氣與生活成本上升影響。能源採購與日圓疲弱推高進口成本，淨出口拖累成長0.6個百分點；企業投資則在AI相關支出支持下增加1.6%。

日本央行審議委員高田創仍主張，升息速度與幅度應保有彈性。目前政策利率為1.25%，已落在央行估計1.1%至2.5%的中性區間，但他認為，利率仍須充分朝中性水準移動，以管理物價與景氣循環風險。他表示，近期經濟發展與AI股下跌，對其看法影響不大。Bloomberg週一報導中，隔夜指數交換定價顯示，12月18日決策升息機率約85%。

SMBC日興的Keita Matsumoto在11月11日受訪時，從部位角度提出另一項觀察。日本國內銀行逐步增持5至10年期日本公債，較長線的海外資產管理機構則與避險基金一同買入超長天期債券。截至11月6日，外資已連續六週買進日本債券，為2020年3月以來最長紀錄。Matsumoto認為，投資人正為殖利率可能下降預作準備，同時也承認通膨與政策仍有不確定性。這些需求已發展數週，與市場持續預期日本央行再度升息並存。

歐洲方面，歐洲央行副總裁Boris Vujcic表示，市場對2027年升息的定價看來並非不合理，但政策路徑尚未預定。投資人押注12月升息一次後，明年再升息兩次、每次25個基點；Bloomberg調查中，多數分析師則預期緊縮將於下個月停止。立陶宛的Gediminas Simkus另表示，是否需要進一步行動，取決於通膨與政策傳導。Vujcic強調，基礎通膨大致穩定，薪資尚未明顯反應，但能源可能推高整體通膨。Bloomberg當日市場報導中，德國10年期殖利率上升1個基點至3.39%，英國上升3個基點至5.36%。

## 增資與新交易反映信用融資冷暖不一

新世界發展擬辦理HK$249億供股，為修復資產負債表引入更具體的家族承諾。新股定價HK$0.90，較停牌前週四收盤折價82%。股價週一盤中最多下跌47%，收盤下跌41%至約HK$2.89，市值降至約$9.25億。

鄭氏家族透過周大福企業，承諾全數認購其45.3%配額，並與負責銷售其餘股份的銀行共同安排，由家族提供最終包底。若少數股東不參與，家族持股可能升至約72.5%。方案擬申請清洗豁免，以免除通常因此觸發的強制全面收購要約義務，獨立股東預定1月5日表決。

執行長Echo Huang表示，約34%所得款項將提前償還既有銀行貸款，36%用於其他債務償付，其餘支持營運資金與專案；若無此方案，流動性與財務彈性將明顯更加吃緊。公司最近一個會計年度虧損$36億，6月底淨負債相當於股東權益106.5%，高於一年前的98%。標普Edward Chan認為，供股與銀行貸款展期若成功，可改善短期流動性。這項融資仍待股東批准，潛在現金紓解將伴隨大幅股權稀釋。

美國槓桿融資的結果分歧。花旗牽頭的銀行團因投資人需求不足，撤回UST Global的$4億再融資案。原擬以五年期貸款償還2028年到期債務，推介條件為基準利率加4.25至4.5個百分點、發行價格98。貸款機構說明會於10月15日舉行，承諾截止日為10月28日，但交易未完成定價；撤案後，公司須另尋再融資途徑。

Thoma Bravo支持的資安公司Proofpoint則開始推介近$20億融資，用於收購及延長債務到期日。其中$12.5億五年期債券用於支持收購Varonis，初步定價落在9%區間低端；另有$7.35億貸款，將到期日由2028年延至2030年，並與7月修訂的$43億定期貸款合併為可互換的同一貸款。擬議貸款利差為美國基準利率加4.5個百分點，折價發行價格為99.27至99.5。兩筆交易均由摩根大通牽頭，貸款承諾週三截止。

CCC Intelligent Solutions也開始推介$6.5億債券，協助GTCR與Elliott收購公司；加上同步進行的貸款，融資總額約$28.5億。借款人力求在感恩節與預期中的政策升息之前取得資金，投資人則仍可拒絕個別交易。

Pizza Hut在另一個市場完成定價，發行$10億整體業務證券化融資，以美國、加拿大及其他地區的加盟契約與權利金等收益資產作支持，協助LongRange Capital收購。最大一部分為$6.65億，加權平均年限4.8年，定價為基準利率加2.65個百分點，票息7.504%；另有$2.35億已預先配售，$1億浮動融資票據則未對外發售。交易預計11月20日交割，預期取得標普及Kroll的BBB評等。瑞銀負責安排此架構，並提供過橋融資。

Alphabet正準備再度運用市政債市場。初步文件顯示，它將是Southeast Energy Authority兩筆預付能源發行的資金接收方，總額$30億，由高盛承銷，參與的公用事業為Salt River Project。這類安排讓接收方先取得債券所得款項，再分期付款，以促成折價能源交付。隨著銀行以外的參與者增加，今年預付能源發行已達約$400億，超越去年$310億紀錄。Alphabet在這兩筆擬議交易之前，已於11月4日完成一筆約$16億交易定價。

Virgin Media O2則再遭信用評等打擊。穆迪因轉型速度不確定，以及£220億債務負擔帶來壓力，將評等下調一級至B2。即使規劃中的節省支出與削減資本支出開始見效，穆迪仍預期信用指標將承壓至2027年。公司目標是在2029年前將每年支出減少£8億。nexfibre擬收購Netomnia的最終競爭審查裁定仍很重要，因為交易可為Virgin Media O2帶來近£10億現金。穆迪同時指出，公司流動性強健、2029年前沒有重大債務到期，眼前融資資源充足，但長期市場融資能力較弱。

## 巴西賣壓與Braskem談判凸顯主權市場分化

巴西里拉週一下跌2.3%，至2025年4月以來最低，魯拉連任以來累計跌幅擴至14%。交換利率飆升，高負債企業的美元債下跌。投資人持續質疑，以增加收入為主的財政措施能否穩住債務走勢，全球風險偏好降溫與油價下跌又增加壓力。Banco StoneX的Marcio Riauba認為，政府重增收而非減支，正在推高風險溢價。

央行每週調查顯示預期進一步惡化。經濟學家將2027年底Selic利率預測由12.5%上修至12.75%，通膨預測由4.9%上修至5%。本月稍早暫停降息後，目前政策利率為13.75%。另外，央行經濟活動指數9月較8月下降0.25%，年減0.01%。預期借款成本提高與活動轉弱同時出現，使高槓桿企業更難調整。

Braskem債務談判提供了具體企業案例。債權人否決最新提案，其中包括股東注資$11億及$29億債轉股；若再加入附條件的$3億股本與$9億債轉股，合計可分別增至$14億及$38億。部分債權人正準備反提案，希望在11月22日協議期限前達成共識，避免公司聲請破產保護。

新提案的基本股本投入低於10月公開方案承諾的$12億，基本債轉股則高於先前最高約$28億。舊方案另規劃，若特定指標需要，可於2029年6月再投入最高$5億股本，並進行$5億至$10億債轉股。差異涉及損失吸收的組成與附帶條件，債權人是否接受仍是關鍵。Braskem表示，進展將透過正式管道公布，目前談判持續進行。

哥倫比亞一方面大量進入融資市場，另一方面在財政政策上讓步。總統Abelardo de la Espriella表示，政府將放棄把加值稅擴及更多商品與服務的計畫。政府正爭取國會支持更廣泛的財政方案，此舉縮減了原擬調整的一部分。

Bloomberg新發布的評估顯示，今年哥倫比亞主權美元債發行已約$100億，為1999年有資料以來最高；10月發行$52億後，Ecopetrol與EPM於本月稍早又合計發行$30億。9月至11月11日企業發債年增209%至$36億，包括GeoPark，同期可比的新興市場企業發行卻下降逾40%。這些已完成的交易，顯示哥倫比亞借款人大力利用新政府上任後的融資窗口。

政府最初提出的2027年預算，赤字占GDP達9.4%，高於前政府預估的4.5%。政府目標是在2030年前將赤字降低逾4個百分點，並將明年外部融資需求由約$280億降至約$150億。國會上月批准支出增加16%，接下來如何處理財政調整仍很重要。知情人士另指出，哥倫比亞正洽談約$150億的國際貨幣基金備用安排。這些協商與擬議削減，仍是未來可能的紓解來源。

其他市場的匯率壓力也加深。印尼盾跌至每美元18,271的歷史低點，週一最多下跌0.4%，今年累計貶值約9%。法國農業信貸銀行Jeffrey Zhang預期印尼央行週三維持利率，認為匯率走勢符合全球金融條件收緊、以及市場預期聯準會加快緊縮的背景。南非因聯合政府穩定性疑慮，蘭特逼近每美元17；一週隱含波動率上升29個基點至11.13%。南非10年期公債殖利率一週上升20個基點至8.77%，地方議會須在11月27日前選出領導人。

經濟學家對印度利率路徑的評估也上移。Bloomberg報導，預期目前5.5%的政策利率還將上升50至75個基點，最高可能達6.25%。匯豐Pranjul Bhandari預期12月升息50個基點，因油價與食品價格衝擊互相強化；ICRA的Aditi Nayar則預期，未來兩個月通膨仍將高於印度央行6%的容忍上限。4至6月GDP成長7.8%、民間消費成長7.1%，提供部分緊縮空間，但成本上升威脅家庭需求，農村尤其如此。

印度銀行資本規範另面臨司法考驗。最高法院10月推翻Yes Bank的840億盧比額外第一類資本（AT1）債券減記，印度央行於11月13日提出覆核，Yes Bank也聲請覆核；債券持有人則提起藐視法庭聲請，要求遵行裁決。銀行表示，若認列判決影響，第2季將由盈轉虧，主要資本比率也可能下降約2.5個百分點。法院認定接管人無權註銷這些證券，影響銀行救援時如何分配損失。

烏拉圭則作出不同的實際政策決定：10月升息後，本次維持6%。央行形容政策仍具擴張性，近期指標未顯示需求面壓力。10月通膨已升至近4.9%，但官員預期仍會落在3%至6%的容忍區間，並在24個月內收斂至4.5%。相較其他市場面臨的緊縮壓力，烏拉圭依不同的國內通膨評估，逐步撤除刺激。

## 後續市場焦點

11月17日將公布下一批美國需求與成本數據。零售銷售預期月增0.6%，前值為0.8%；ADP每週就業數據前次增加19,750人。紐約聯準銀行服務業活動指數預期為負6，前值負20.7。製造業已呈現訂單轉弱、僱用增強，這些數據將擴大對其他部門的觀察。進口物價預期月增1.7%，前值1.1%；出口物價預期月增1.4%，前值2.2%，將分別檢驗外部成本壓力。

週三公布的聯準會10月會議紀錄，將揭示當時維持利率不變、但有兩位官員主張升息而反對的討論。Hammack新近提出勞動市場轉緊與持續轉嫁成本的跡象，使官員對接連小幅升息的支持有多廣泛，格外重要。美國財政部11月18日標售20年期公債，11月19日標售10年期TIPS，將在實質殖利率再度上升後檢驗承接需求。

Nvidia將於週二美股收盤後公布業績，其展望與客戶支持說明，將直接影響評等較弱雲端業者取得租約與融資的能力。Anthropic預計週三定價、週四開始交易，訂單約為可供認購股份的7倍，連同另一筆私募，計畫募資$904億。供應商擔保與舉債能力受到更嚴格檢視之際，這些需求能否轉成資金，將檢驗公開股票市場的融資能力。Proofpoint週三的貸款承諾截止，則是另一項近期槓桿融資需求指標。

Braskem的11月22日期限已近，債權人要求、股東出資與債轉股之間須儘快取得共識。新世界發展1月5日的股東表決，則是較晚、且不同的資本重整批准條件。兩案討論中的條款，都決定借款人可取得多少流動性紓解，以及成本由哪些資金提供者承擔。

印尼央行週三決策緊接印尼盾創低，分析師目前對維持利率或可能升息看法分歧。英國週二勞動數據與週三CPI將檢驗12月緊縮預期；CPI預期為3.6%，本週前瞻的勞動市場報導預估失業率4.7%。歐洲央行週三發布《金融穩定評估》，將進一步說明Vujcic對AI債務曝險、主權脆弱性及非銀行機構相互連結的警告。歐洲領袖另預計在11月26至27日高峰會討論歐洲央行總裁與兩個理事職缺，西班牙正推動就Pablo Hernandez de Cos的人選達成共識。

川普、習近平與普丁預計週四於深圳會晤，讓能源外交與科技限制，和產業融資考驗集中在同一週。美國政府表示將討論伊朗，川普也說打算談烏克蘭及核武軍控。供應安全或先進運算使用權若有具體變化，影響將超越股市即時反應。中國12月經濟政策會議則將提供另一個觀察點：10月投資萎縮後，官員打算如何把舉債額度與可用財政資源化為實際支出。

overall_summary.headline: 油價下跌壓低通膨補償，美債小幅回升，實質殖利率仍走高
overall_summary.session_narrative:
科技股再度遭到拋售、油價下跌約4%，美債僅小幅回升。10年期殖利率下降0.41個基點至5.1311%，2年期下降1.25個基點至4.8294%，30年期則上升0.86個基點至5.4741%。名目殖利率的喘息來自通膨補償回落：10年期損益兩平通膨率下降3.48個基點至2.2157%，實質殖利率仍上升3.07個基點至2.9154%。

克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack仍傾向接連小幅升息，並指出勞動市場開始轉緊、更多企業計畫轉嫁成本。長期通膨預期穩固受控，讓政策保有漸進調整的空間。紐約州製造業調查也呈現同樣的混合訊號：訂單轉弱，僱用卻增強。

再融資與AI信用支持受到檢視，美國高收益債利差明顯擴大。銀行因需求不足撤回UST Global的$4億再融資案；Proofpoint開始推介用於收購與延長到期日的債務，Pizza Hut則完成加盟業務支持融資的定價。Nvidia力求限制租約義務，使評等較弱雲端業者能獲得多少支持受到質疑。新世界發展擬辦理HK$249億供股，以家族支持換取流動性紓解，但股權稀釋代價高昂。

中國10月活動數據疲弱，同時出現中期流動性回收與公債下跌；日本GDP萎縮，也未改變高田創主張升息的看法。接下來的美國需求與成本數據、聯準會會議紀錄，以及Nvidia對客戶支持的說明，將檢驗政策緊縮與融資壓力之間的平衡。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries recovered only modestly as another sharp technology-stock selloff and falling oil prices met a Federal Reserve still preparing to tighten policy. The 10-year yield edged down 0.41 basis point to 5.1311%, while the two-year fell 1.25 basis points to 4.8294%. U.S. high-yield spreads widened noticeably as investors confronted more immediate questions about refinancing access and the financial support underpinning the AI construction boom.

The small nominal-yield decline concealed a further increase in real borrowing costs. Inflation compensation fell as crude dropped about 4%, but the 10-year real yield rose. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack supplied a fresh reason for caution: although she continued to favor successive small rate increases, she reported emerging signs of tighter labor conditions and more businesses planning to pass on costs. Longer-run inflation expectations remained well anchored in her assessment, preserving room for a measured approach.

The financing news was more differentiated than the equity retreat. Banks withdrew UST Global's refinancing after inadequate investor demand, while Proofpoint began marketing acquisition and maturity-extension debt and Pizza Hut priced franchise-backed financing. In Asia, New World Development's proposed recapitalization brought a substantial Cheng-family commitment alongside severe dilution for minority shareholders. China's weak October activity figures coincided with a medium-term liquidity withdrawal and losses in government debt, showing that disappointing growth was not translating immediately into easier funding conditions.

## Treasury Relief Meets a Broader Inflation Warning

The strongest Treasury gains were in intermediate maturities. The five-year yield declined 2.16 basis points to 4.94%, while the 30-year rose 0.86 basis point to 5.4741%. The two- to 10-year curve steepened 0.84 basis point to 30.17 basis points; the two- to 30-year gap widened 2.11 basis points to 64.47. Shorter maturities found some relief after the previous week's repricing, but the long bond did not participate in the recovery.

The weekly comparison still showed a substantial increase in yields. Two- and five-year yields were 26.79 and 26.33 basis points above November 9, respectively, against increases of 24.91 basis points at 10 years and 19.58 at 30 years. Over a month, the two-year was up 12.11 basis points and the 10-year 5.83. Monday's move therefore reduced only a small portion of the recent rise in policy-sensitive borrowing costs.

Real yields and inflation compensation pulled in opposite directions. The 10-year TIPS yield increased 3.07 basis points to 2.9154%, while the breakeven fell 3.48 basis points to 2.2157%. Over the week, the real yield was up 25.89 basis points and the breakeven down 0.98; over a month, the corresponding changes were an increase of 19.34 and a decline of 13.51 basis points. The inflation-compensation retreat allowed nominal debt to stabilize even as the real discount rate facing long-lived investments continued to rise.

Oil supplied a clear source of relief on the price side. WTI futures fell 3.95% to $85.06 a barrel and Brent lost 4.17% to $91.84, leaving both about 14% below their month-earlier levels. Bloomberg's market account attributed the decline to ample physical supplies and expectations of a growing surplus, which outweighed concern about Middle East disruption. Iran's renewed attacks on Bahrain kept geopolitical risk active, while the prospect of diplomatic discussions and President Donald Trump's reluctance to escalate attacks reduced the immediate pressure on crude. Saxo Bank's Ole Sloth Hansen said the supply-surplus outlook was carrying more weight unless tensions produced actual supply losses.

Hammack's Monday remarks addressed the conditions that could upset a gradual tightening path. The Cleveland president, an October dissenter in favor of an increase, continued to prefer small, steady moves at successive meetings. She said an inflationary mindset taking hold among businesses and consumers could require larger steps and a higher eventual destination. Her assessment of current policy was at or slightly below neutral, leaving more restraint necessary to curb investment at the margin.

Her concern extended beyond energy and tariffs. Hammack identified demand from AI infrastructure and other growth as additional inflation sources. More managers were discussing further price increases, some businesses were raising wages at the lower end of the income distribution, and district contacts reported difficulty finding skilled and unskilled workers. In core services excluding housing, she emphasized fully loaded employment costs, including benefits and health insurance, as a source of pressure. Those observations sharpened the labor-cost dimension of the debate over how broadly inflation is spreading.

She also preserved an important qualification: longer-run inflation expectations remained well anchored around the Fed's objective. Market expectations of near-term increases and low longer-term inflation supported her view that credibility remained strong and officials had time to choose the pace. She did not anticipate that restoring price stability would require a significant labor-market impact, citing continued strong growth and firms' ability to pass costs to other businesses as signs that demand was not yet constrained.

The November Empire State manufacturing survey offered a similarly mixed picture of slower activity and persistent resource demand. Trading Economics reported that the general business conditions index fell to 7.8 from 25.5, below the 18 consensus. The positive reading still indicated expansion, following October's strongest result since December 2021. New orders slowed sharply to 3 from 23.2, and shipments registered 8.8.

Hiring moved the other way. Employment rose to 18.1 from 10.3, its fastest growth in more than four years, and the workweek increased to 13.5 from 9.1. Prices paid eased to 45.9 from 59.5 and prices received to 27.2 from 30.6, leaving both elevated. Slower orders were consequently accompanied by stronger labor demand and less intense, but continuing, price increases.

Supply conditions improved unevenly. Delivery times eased to 13.8 from 19.8, while supply availability improved to minus 9.2 from minus 15.1. Unfilled orders declined to 10.3 from 14 and inventories to 9.2 from 11.6. Firms became more optimistic about the outlook: future conditions rose to 28.9 from 21, and capital-spending plans to 23 from 14. The survey's weaker headline gave bond investors a softer activity observation without removing the investment and employment strength relevant to Hammack's argument.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's separate Monday appearance concentrated on AI contingencies. Staff are examining an expansion that distributes productivity gains between employers and workers, another in which increased activity coexists with massive job losses, and a disappointment scenario involving lower equity valuations, economic weakness and higher unemployment. He explicitly described these as scenarios rather than forecasts and offered no direct near-term rate guidance. The exercise leaves the timing and distribution of AI's benefits open while the Fed assesses its already visible investment demand.

## AI Credit Support Comes Under Closer Scrutiny

The equity selloff intensified the financing questions surrounding the AI industry. The S&P 500 fell 1.92%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 2.67% and the semiconductor index dropped 5.28%. The VIX rose 18.70% to 22.91. Nvidia shares declined 4.1%, while renewed weakness in neocloud companies focused attention on the guarantees and lease arrangements that have helped them obtain data-center capacity.

Washington added a concrete restriction on the industry's international business. The Commerce Department moved to limit Chinese companies' remote access to advanced AI chips and servers. Data-center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil will be required to obtain licenses to buy semiconductors from Nvidia and other U.S. suppliers. The rule reaches access to computing capacity as well as the physical destination of chips, widening the commercial issues facing the sector after Nvidia's leadership upheaval.

Trump supported calls for Jensen Huang's reinstatement, while CNBC reported that Nvidia's board was not considering bringing him back. The disagreement leaves strategy with interim CEO Colette Kress and the eventual successor. For lenders and landlords, a central question is how that management team will handle support for companies that buy Nvidia equipment but have weaker standalone credit profiles.

Bloomberg's new reporting described a retreat from assuming full lease obligations that was already under way before Huang's departure. Nvidia had been seeking less burdensome guarantees, limiting upfront balance-sheet commitments and the obligations it would face if a neocloud failed to honor a lease. Needham analyst John Todaro said chipmaker support had become more necessary, making uncertainty over its continuation consequential for credit availability.

The Dalton, Georgia, negotiations illustrated the practical limits. Earlier this year, CoreWeave and Nvidia discussed Nvidia taking lease obligations to help secure additional space from Core Scientific, and bankers considered financing around the arrangement. Nvidia ultimately did not provide that backing, people familiar with the matter said; AMD subsequently filled the space as part of a broader July agreement with Core Scientific.

CoreWeave said it chose not to pursue the extra capacity. It also said it had not used third-party support from Nvidia or another partner to secure investment-grade wraps for its data centers, and described a path from roughly 1.7 gigawatts of active power to more than 8 gigawatts by 2030. Core Scientific disputed Bloomberg's reporting without further explanation and said customer diversification had been a business priority. Those responses matter to the interpretation of a transaction that did not materialize.

Landlords' credit requirements are another constraint. TeraWulf, which accepts investment-grade tenants or credit support from blue-chip partners, declined to consider CoreWeave when it could not satisfy those conditions, according to people familiar with the matter. Applied Digital is capping exposure to non-investment-grade customers at 30% of capacity after signing large CoreWeave leases last year. The restrictions connect tenant credit quality directly to the ability to expand physical capacity.

CoreWeave fell as much as 8.6% Monday and Nebius as much as 9.6%. The new declines extended pressure on companies whose funding models depend on building capacity before collecting the full stream of customer revenues. Nvidia's support takes different forms across those relationships: it committed $2 billion to help Nebius adopt its infrastructure, has discussed credit guarantees for an Nscale facility intended for Anthropic, and pledged as much as $105 billion in support for the Ohio project leased by OpenAI from SB Energy. The specific commitments and negotiations differ substantially in size and legal form.

Fresh official assessments expanded the focus beyond market valuations. Fed Governor Michael Barr warned in prepared remarks for a Milan conference that autonomous AI agents could accelerate deposit flight by identifying yield differences or stability signals and moving money within minutes. Major banks are already detecting attempts by agents to take unauthorized actions in retail accounts, he said. His proposed safeguards included specific consent verification and technical limits on agent capabilities. Barr also pointed to more than $3 trillion of off-balance-sheet liabilities and circular financing arrangements in AI infrastructure as vulnerabilities.

A new paper by four Fed economists gave a separate macroeconomic assessment. Large-scale capital expenditure was already affecting GDP and prices, while employment effects remained small and mixed. Much of the recent improvement in productivity predated widespread generative-AI adoption. Prolonged shortages of materials and labor for data centers could intensify inflation, the authors argued, while larger eventual productivity gains could be disinflationary. Their finding helps explain why current construction demand and future supply gains can carry different policy implications.

Institutional allocation changes supplied a counterpoint to the retreat in shares. BlackRock raised the equity overweight in its model portfolios to 3% from 1%, broadened AI exposure and added longer-duration government bonds while tactically rebuilding credit holdings, especially in bond-heavy portfolios. Michael Gates, who leads its Target Allocation ETF models, said credit was not broadly cheap and rates could remain volatile. Over the latest two sessions, GOVT lost roughly $4.4 billion and IUSB more than $1 billion, while the systematic bond fund SYSB received about $600 million. Those reallocations accompanied changes within fixed income as well as the increase in equity exposure.

## Weak Asian Data Do Not Deliver Immediate Easing

China's October releases showed a broad loss of momentum after September's support measures. Retail sales increased just 0.4% from a year earlier, below the 0.8% consensus, while industrial output grew 4.8% and slowed for the first time in three months. Fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in January-October, against a 7% decline expected in Bloomberg's survey. Bloomberg Economics estimated a 17% annual contraction for October alone, the sharpest outside the pandemic.

The investment deterioration came after additional borrowing authority and an 800 billion-yuan construction-support program. BofA's Helen Qiao described a waiting period before stimulus took effect and suggested officials might be conserving some support for weaker conditions in 2027 and 2028. Goldman Sachs economists pointed to unusually strong growth in government bank deposits in October as a sign that some money raised in Q4 might not be spent until early 2027. The gap between funding and actual expenditure is central to whether fiscal measures can reverse the investment decline.

The composition showed how much strength remained concentrated in AI-related production. Electronics manufacturing rose nearly 20% annually, while car production increased only 0.9%, its weakest growth since the end of Covid. Property investment fell 21.6% in the first 10 months, worsening from a 20.6% decline through September. New-home prices in 70 cities excluding subsidized housing dropped 0.15% monthly after 0.14%; resale prices fell 0.24% after 0.26%.

The urban surveyed unemployment rate improved to 5.1% from 5.2%. Economists cited in Bloomberg's account cautioned that the measure excludes migrant workers who return to the countryside after losing jobs. With GDP up 4.6% in the first three quarters, the economy would need 4.3% growth in Q4 to reach the lower end of the official 4.5%-5% annual target. That arithmetic gives officials some tolerance for slower activity, even as the concentration of growth raises questions about domestic demand.

The PBOC's liquidity operation added a different signal to the bond market. It provided 200 billion yuan through six-month outright reverse repos against 300 billion yuan of maturities. Together with the earlier three-month operation, Bloomberg calculated a net withdrawal of 300 billion yuan through the tool this month, the first such drain since June. Overnight bank funding rose to 1.30%, compared with a six-month low of 1.25% earlier in November. The 10-year sovereign yield increased 1 basis point to 1.62%, and 30-year bond futures fell 0.9% to their lowest since September 18.

Golden Credit Rating's Wang Qing said the withdrawal would restrain further declines in overnight rates and prevent operational reforms from being read as a rate cut. Concern over credit incidents added to the pressure: QiaoYin City Management had warned of a possible delay in convertible-bond repayment before promising to remit funds Tuesday. The central bank separately injected funds through overnight reverse repos Monday, and Wang said medium-term injections could resume at year-end to accommodate government issuance and bank lending. The combination points to selective liquidity management rather than a simple response to the weak growth release.

Hong Kong meanwhile introduced infrastructure for a rapidly expanding offshore funding market. HKEX launched its first bond index, tracking offshore renminbi bonds listed on the exchange or settled through the Central Moneymarkets Unit. Bloomberg Index Services will administer and calculate it. Sovereign and corporate dim sum issuance has reached about 1.2 trillion yuan, or $175 billion, this year, already exceeding the full-year 2025 total. The index accompanies official efforts to develop the offshore yuan curve and broaden collateral use.

Japan's GDP release exposed a different tension between consumption and investment. Q3 output contracted 0.1% annualized, worse than the 0.2% expansion expected, as consumer spending fell 0.3%. Bad weather and higher living costs weighed on households. Net exports subtracted 0.6 percentage point as energy procurement and the weak yen increased import costs, while corporate investment rose 1.6% with support from AI-related spending.

BOJ board member Hajime Takata nevertheless advocated flexibility in both the pace and size of increases. The policy rate stands at 1.25%, within the central bank's estimated 1.1%-2.5% neutral range, but he argued it needed to move sufficiently toward neutral to manage price and business-cycle risks. He said recent economic developments and the AI-stock decline had changed his view little. Overnight-indexed swaps implied roughly an 85% chance of an increase at the December 18 decision in Bloomberg's Monday account.

SMBC Nikko's Keita Matsumoto offered a separate positioning assessment based on a November 11 interview. Domestic banks were gradually extending into five- to 10-year JGBs, while longer-term foreign asset managers were joining hedge funds in superlong debt. Foreign investors had bought Japanese debt for six successive weeks through November 6, the longest run since March 2020. Matsumoto saw investors preparing for potentially lower yields, while acknowledging inflation and policy uncertainty. That assessment describes demand developing over several weeks alongside continued expectations of another BOJ increase.

In Europe, ECB Vice President Boris Vujcic said market pricing of a 2027 increase did not appear unreasonable, although no policy path was predetermined. Investors were betting on two quarter-point moves next year after one in December, while most analysts in Bloomberg's survey expected tightening to stop next month. Lithuania's Gediminas Simkus separately said further action might be needed depending on inflation and policy transmission. Vujcic emphasized that underlying inflation was broadly stable and wages were not yet responding materially, while energy could push headline inflation higher. Germany's 10-year yield rose 1 basis point to 3.39% in Bloomberg's session account; Britain's increased 3 basis points to 5.36%.

## Recapitalizations and New Deals Reveal Uneven Credit Access

New World Development's proposed HK$24.9 billion rights issue put a more concrete family commitment behind efforts to repair its balance sheet. The new shares are priced at HK$0.90, an 82% discount to Thursday's close before the trading halt. The stock fell as much as 47% Monday and closed 41% lower near HK$2.89, cutting market capitalization to about $925 million.

Through Chow Tai Fook Enterprises, the Cheng family committed to taking its full 45.3% allotment and is serving as the ultimate backstop alongside banks selling the remaining shares. Its ownership could rise to about 72.5% if minority investors do not participate. A proposed whitewash waiver would exempt it from the mandatory general offer that would normally be triggered. Independent shareholders are due to vote January 5.

CEO Echo Huang said about 34% of proceeds would prepay existing bank loans, 36% would go to broader debt servicing, and the balance would support working capital and projects. She said liquidity and financial flexibility would be materially tighter without the plan. The developer reported a $3.6 billion loss in its latest fiscal year, and net debt reached 106.5% of shareholder equity at June-end, against 98% a year earlier. S&P's Edward Chan said the proposed rights issue and bank-loan extensions could improve near-term liquidity if successful. The financing offers potential cash relief at a substantial dilution cost, with shareholder approval still ahead.

U.S. leveraged finance showed divergent outcomes. Citigroup-led banks pulled UST Global's $400 million refinancing after insufficient investor demand. The proposed five-year loan would have refinanced debt due in 2028 and had been marketed at 4.25-4.5 percentage points over the benchmark, with an issue price of 98. A lender call took place October 15 and commitments were due October 28, but the transaction did not price. Its withdrawal leaves the company seeking a different route to that refinancing.

Proofpoint began marketing nearly $2 billion for acquisition funding and a maturity extension. The Thoma Bravo-backed cybersecurity company offered a $1.25 billion five-year bond to support its Varonis acquisition, with initial pricing in the low 9% area. A $735 million loan would extend debt to 2030 from 2028 and become fungible with its $4.3 billion term loan amended in July. The proposed loan margin is 4.5 percentage points over the U.S. benchmark, at a discounted price of 99.27-99.5. JPMorgan is leading both transactions, with loan commitments due Wednesday.

CCC Intelligent Solutions separately began marketing $650 million of bonds to help finance its buyout by GTCR and Elliott. Together with a concurrent loan, the package would total about $2.85 billion. Borrowers are trying to secure funding before Thanksgiving and ahead of expected policy increases, while investors retain the ability to reject individual deals.

Pizza Hut achieved pricing in a different market. It sold a $1 billion whole-business securitization backed by revenue-producing assets, including franchise agreements and royalties in the U.S., Canada and other locations, to help fund its LongRange Capital buyout. The largest portion, $665 million with a 4.8-year weighted-average life, priced at 2.65 percentage points over benchmarks with a 7.504% coupon. Another $235 million was pre-placed and a $100 million variable funding note was not offered. Closing is expected November 20, with BBB ratings expected from S&P and Kroll. UBS led the structure and provided bridge financing.

Alphabet is preparing another use of the municipal market. Preliminary documents identify it as funding recipient for two Southeast Energy Authority prepaid-energy offerings totaling $3 billion, managed by Goldman Sachs. Salt River Project is the participating utility. In these arrangements, the recipient obtains bond proceeds upfront and makes payments over time facilitating discounted energy delivery. Annual prepaid-energy issuance has reached about $40 billion, above last year's $31 billion record, as participation broadens beyond banks. Alphabet's proposed transactions follow a roughly $1.6 billion deal priced November 4.

Virgin Media O2 received a fresh credit setback. Moody's cut its rating one notch to B2 amid uncertainty over the pace of its turnaround and pressure from a £22 billion debt burden. It expects credit metrics to remain strained through 2027 even as planned savings and capital-expenditure reductions begin producing benefits. The company aims to cut annual expenditures by £800 million by 2029. A final competition ruling on nexfibre's proposed Netomnia acquisition remains important because the deal would bring Virgin Media O2 nearly £1 billion of cash. Moody's also cited strong liquidity and no major maturities before 2029, distinguishing immediate funding resources from weaker long-term market access.

## Brazil's Selloff and Braskem Talks Deepen Sovereign Differentiation

Brazil's real fell 2.3% Monday to its weakest since April 2025, extending its decline since Lula's reelection to 14%. Swap rates surged and dollar bonds of highly indebted companies declined. Investors continued to question whether revenue-focused fiscal measures could stabilize the debt trajectory, with the global retreat in risk appetite and lower oil adding pressure. Banco StoneX's Marcio Riauba said the emphasis on raising revenue rather than cutting spending was contributing to risk premiums.

The central bank's weekly survey captured a fresh deterioration in expectations. Economists raised their end-2027 Selic forecast to 12.75% from 12.5% and inflation to 5% from 4.9%. The current policy rate is 13.75%, following the pause in easing earlier this month. Separately, the central bank's activity index fell 0.25% in September from August and 0.01% annually. Higher expected borrowing costs are arriving alongside weaker activity, complicating the adjustment for leveraged businesses.

Braskem's debt negotiations supplied a specific corporate consequence. Creditors rejected its latest proposal, which included $1.1 billion of shareholder equity and $2.9 billion of debt conversion. Conditional additions of $300 million in equity and $900 million in conversion could bring the totals to $1.4 billion and $3.8 billion. Some creditors are preparing a counterproposal ahead of the November 22 deadline for an agreement intended to avert a bankruptcy-protection filing.

The revised base equity contribution was below the $1.2 billion commitment in October's public proposal, while base conversion exceeded the earlier amount of up to about $2.8 billion. That earlier plan also contemplated up to $500 million of additional equity and $500 million-$1 billion of conversion in June 2029 if needed for specified metrics. The differences involve the mix and conditionality of loss absorption, leaving creditor acceptance central. Braskem said developments would be disclosed through official channels; negotiations remain ongoing.

Colombia's financing picture combined substantial market access with a fiscal concession. President Abelardo de la Espriella said the government was abandoning plans to extend value-added tax to more goods and services. That narrows an element of the proposed adjustment while the administration seeks legislative backing for its broader fiscal program.

Bloomberg's newly published assessment quantified the scale of borrowing already undertaken: roughly $10 billion of sovereign dollar issuance this year, the most since its data begin in 1999. October's $5.2 billion sale was followed by $3 billion from Ecopetrol and EPM earlier this month. Corporate sales from September through November 11 rose 209% annually to $3.6 billion, including GeoPark, even as comparable emerging-market corporate issuance fell more than 40%. These historical transactions show how strongly Colombian borrowers have used the window available to the new administration.

The government's initial 2027 budget put the deficit at 9.4% of GDP, compared with its predecessor's 4.5% projection. It aims to reduce the deficit by more than 4 percentage points by 2030 and lower next year's external financing requirement toward $15 billion from about $28 billion. Congress's treatment of the adjustment remains consequential after lawmakers approved a 16% spending increase last month. Colombia is also negotiating a potential IMF stand-by arrangement of about $15 billion, according to people familiar with the discussions. Those negotiations and proposed reductions remain prospective sources of relief.

Currency pressure also sharpened elsewhere. Indonesia's rupiah reached a record 18,271 per dollar, down as much as 0.4% Monday and about 9% this year. Credit Agricole's Jeffrey Zhang expected Bank Indonesia to hold Wednesday, judging the currency move consistent with tighter global conditions and faster Fed tightening expectations. South Africa's rand approached 17 per dollar amid concern over coalition stability; one-week implied volatility rose 29 basis points to 11.13%. Its 10-year government yield had increased 20 basis points over the week to 8.77%, while councils face a November 27 deadline to elect leadership.

India's prospective rate path moved higher in economists' assessments. Bloomberg reported expectations for another 50-75 basis points from the current 5.5%, potentially taking the benchmark to 6.25%. HSBC's Pranjul Bhandari expected a 50-basis-point December increase as oil and food shocks reinforce each other. ICRA's Aditi Nayar expected inflation to remain above the RBI's 6% tolerance ceiling over the next couple of months. The growth backdrop provides some room to tighten, with April-June GDP up 7.8% and private consumption 7.1%, although higher costs threaten household demand, particularly in rural areas.

India's banking-capital rules face a separate legal test. The RBI sought review on November 13 of the Supreme Court's October decision overturning Yes Bank's 84 billion-rupee AT1 write-off. Yes Bank also requested review, while bondholders filed a contempt petition seeking compliance. The lender said recognizing the ruling would have turned its second-quarter result into a loss and could reduce its key capital ratio by about 2.5 percentage points. The court's finding that the administrator lacked authority to extinguish the securities has implications for how bank-rescue losses can be allocated.

Uruguay delivered a contrasting realized decision, holding at 6% after October's increase. The central bank described policy as expansionary and saw no demand-side pressure in recent indicators. Inflation had risen to nearly 4.9% in October, but officials expected it to stay within the 3%-6% tolerance band and converge toward 4.5% over 24 months. Its measured withdrawal of stimulus rests on a different domestic inflation assessment from the tightening pressures elsewhere.

## Forward Market Significance

November 17 brings the next U.S. demand and cost observations. Retail sales are forecast to rise 0.6% monthly after 0.8%, while weekly ADP employment follows a 19,750 increase. The New York Fed services activity index is forecast at minus 6 after minus 20.7. Those releases will broaden the picture beyond manufacturing, where weaker orders coexisted with stronger hiring. Import prices are forecast to rise 1.7% monthly after 1.1%, and export prices 1.4% after 2.2%, adding separate tests of external cost pressure.

Wednesday's October Fed minutes will provide the discussion behind a hold opposed by two officials seeking an increase. Hammack's new evidence of emerging labor tightness and continued cost pass-through makes the breadth of support for successive small increases particularly relevant. Treasury's November 18 sale of 20-year bonds and November 19 sale of 10-year inflation-protected securities will bring demand tests after another increase in real yields.

Nvidia reports after Tuesday's U.S. equity close. Its outlook and discussion of customer support will bear directly on the ability of weaker-rated cloud operators to obtain leases and financing. Anthropic is expected to price Wednesday and begin trading Thursday, with orders around seven times the available shares and a planned $90.4 billion raising including a separate private placement. The conversion of that demand into funding will test access to public equity at a time when supplier guarantees and debt capacity are under closer scrutiny. Proofpoint's Wednesday loan commitments provide a separate near-term measure of leveraged-finance demand.

Braskem's November 22 deadline leaves little time to reconcile creditor demands with shareholder contributions and debt conversion. New World's January 5 shareholder vote is a later, distinct approval condition for its recapitalization. In both cases, the terms under discussion determine how much liquidity relief reaches the borrower and which capital providers absorb the cost.

Bank Indonesia's Wednesday decision follows the rupiah's new low, with current analyst expectations divided between a hold and a possible increase. Britain's Tuesday labor figures and Wednesday CPI will test expectations for December tightening; the latter is expected at 3.6%, while the week-ahead labor account anticipates unemployment of 4.7%. The ECB's Financial Stability Review Wednesday will develop Vujcic's warnings about AI debt exposures, sovereign fragility and non-bank interconnections. Separately, European leaders are expected to address the ECB presidency and two board vacancies at their November 26-27 summit, with Spain pressing for agreement on Pablo Hernandez de Cos.

Thursday's expected Trump-Xi-Putin meeting in Shenzhen brings energy diplomacy and technology restrictions into the same week as the industry's financing tests. The administration has said Iran will be discussed, while Trump has also said he intends to raise Ukraine and nuclear arms control. Concrete changes to supply security or access to advanced computing would carry consequences beyond the immediate stock-market reaction. China's December economic-policy gathering will provide a separate test of how officials intend to turn borrowing authority and available fiscal resources into spending after October's investment contraction.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries recover modestly as falling oil lowers inflation compensation and real yields rise
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries recovered only modestly amid another technology-stock selloff and an oil decline of about 4%. The 10-year yield fell 0.41 basis point to 5.1311% and the 2-year declined 1.25 basis points to 4.8294%, while the 30-year rose 0.86 basis point to 5.4741%. Falling inflation compensation accounted for the nominal-yield relief: the 10-year breakeven declined 3.48 basis points to 2.2157%, even as the real yield increased 3.07 basis points to 2.9154%.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack continued to favor successive small rate increases and reported emerging labor tightness and more businesses planning cost pass-through. Well-anchored longer-run inflation expectations preserved room for a measured approach. The Empire State survey reinforced the mixed picture, with weaker orders alongside stronger hiring.

U.S. high-yield spreads widened noticeably as refinancing and AI credit support came under scrutiny. Banks withdrew UST Global's $400 million refinancing for insufficient demand; Proofpoint began marketing acquisition and maturity-extension debt, and Pizza Hut priced franchise-backed financing. Nvidia's efforts to limit lease obligations raised questions about support for weaker-rated cloud operators. New World's proposed HK$24.9 billion rights issue offered family-backed liquidity relief at a substantial dilution cost.

China's weak October activity figures coincided with a medium-term liquidity withdrawal and government-bond losses. Japan's GDP contraction also left Takata's tightening argument intact. Upcoming U.S. demand and cost data, Fed minutes and Nvidia's customer-support discussion will test the balance between policy restraint and financing pressure.
